title: Counterpart · Foundry study
summary:
**Original lore · provisional**

A foundry builds the left half of a chassis against a sheet of polished steel. At the end of the shift, the workers switch off the lights and listen. On a successful night, the riveting continues. By morning there’s a complete frame on the stand.

From across the arena it looks like military hardware. Up close, you notice that both knees have the same dent, both booster housings have the same crooked weld, and the serial number on the right side is stamped backward.

**Its giveaway is the landing.** After a sideways boost, the loaded knee bends to take the weight. The airborne knee bends by exactly the same amount. For half a second you see the reflection operating inside an otherwise convincing machine.

items.title: Counterpart in the intake bay
items.alt: A dark industrial mech with mirrored crescent scars on its knee guards, an amber rangefinder, four different weapons and a blue jet at one hip. One steel foot is lifted.
items.body:
The crooked collar welds and crescent marks on the pale knee guards repeat across the centerline. One amber sensor and a towing shackle give the low cockpit a face-like expression. Graphite sleeves stretch over the upper legs and fold behind the exposed knee pivots.

A linear rifle and a plasma thrower occupy the hands. A slab missile cassette and twin cannon sit on separate back pivots. The deep booster bells clear the back weapons, and a short blue jet marks the lateral hip nozzle. The lifted foot shows the proposed mirrored landing pose.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/counterpart/foundry-v001.png)
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Paint a single definitive full-body game character portrait of COUNTERPART, an original piloted industrial combat mech. The left half of its frame was fabricated against a sheet of polished steel. The other half came back from the mirror bearing the identical wear in reverse. The four issued weapons were fitted afterward and are conspicuously asymmetric. Make this visual paradox legible without words. One solitary mech; no literal mirror or second figure.

Camera and staging: portrait 4:5 or a near-square frame generous enough for the loadout; near-frontal three-quarter, only 12–15 degrees off center so we can compare the knees and inspect the rangefinder face. Camera at human eye height with modest upward perspective, full figure from the highest two back units to the soles, equipment never cropped. Big, clean graphic silhouette. The setting is a pale, cavernous foundry intake bay with one distant human-sized service door, faded floor lines and cold window light. Calm background, sharp mech details. Arrest the instant just after a short side boost: one boot receives the weight and bites into grit, the other hovers just above the floor, with both knees eerily flexed through the SAME angle despite one being unloaded. Keep the stance balanced and alert, no exaggerated kneeling. The upper chassis stays level.

Chassis identity: a lean 8-metre fighting vehicle. Compact low forward-projecting cockpit like the nose of a military survey instrument, an inclined armored windscreen shutter with a small access hatch and rungs. A small transverse rangefinder head sits low in front, tucked between collar plates. Two practical inspection shutters, one slightly open on an amber optic and one closed, above a single central steel towing socket: a worried expression seen by chance in actual hardware. Keep the head boxy and mechanical. Narrow articulated waist, restrained shoulder armor, large protected hip bearings, long load-bearing legs whose smooth graphite-colored artificial muscle sleeves curve continuously over thighs and calves like a sprinter's legs carrying a heavy machine. Exposed black steel knee pivots, hardened heel links, blunt split steel boots. Compact articulated gun-hands, broad wrist coupling and individual fingers. The torso and hips house a pilot; legs should feel uncomfortably alive but clearly machine-scale. No bare flesh, skull head, demonic horns, glowing runes, Gothic cathedral ornament, angel wings, insect shells or human suit proportions.

Make the ritual's fingerprints LARGE ENOUGH to spot: give both pale steel knee guards the exact same distinctive crescent dent crossed by three diagonal scratches, precisely mirror reversed, and the same crooked copper-colored repair weld repeated in mirror image on both collar plates. Tiny worn two-character factory stamps (17 normal and mirrored on the other side) are optional. The paired damage reads even without lettering. Use faded midnight petrol-blue and gunmetal frame armor, isolated chalk-gray knee guards, one or two old zinc-yellow maintenance marks, graphite limb sleeves; dark red oxide visible beneath worn edges. Controlled wear, vary large flat surfaces and selectively dense fittings. 

Exactly four bold, visually separated, modular mech weapons in the Armored Core tradition: the mech's right hand (image left) grips a long, rectangular industrial linear rifle with an open channel down its squared barrel, lowered slightly outboard. The left hand (image right) grips a much shorter and wider plasma thrower, with a round ceramic-lined emitter and heat-stained shroud, held low and clear of the leg. The shoulders carry TWO independent back-mounted assemblies on visible offset hinged pylons: above one shoulder a squat slab missile cassette showing a recessed grid of dark launch cells, over the opposite shoulder a folded twin-barrel cannon, its two long bores distinguishable. Each weapon reads larger than a person. Low on the back below these pylons, paired deep booster bells peep out around the waist, their heat-darkened segmented skirts visible in profile; separately a small flush lateral maneuvering nozzle at either outer hip, one with a wisp of rapidly fading cold-blue exhaust. Keep the boosters clear of the four weapons. Focus on their mass, not muzzle effects. Rounded organic legs against severely machined specular equipment.

Art direction: a severe, beautiful industrial military concept painting, strong art-directed design, painterly lost edges in the background and exact hard edges at the face, hands, matched knee scars and weapon silhouettes, subtle analog film grain. Cool overcast sidelight and soft fill preserve shape in dark materials. Unsettling, deliberate, battle-worn. No poster captions, no HUD, no diagrams or multi-panel breakdown.

items.title: References used
items.body:
The dark flexing limbs informed how the long legs carry the weight of the cockpit. The marked, mismatched armor informed the battered plates and finish. Both pins were cited in Counterpart’s original pitch. [Random Ghost limb study](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568823387/) · [Garbaldy armor study](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568822614/)

Armored Core informed the four separate weapon positions, hinged back mounts, low rear booster bells and flush outer-hip jets. The mirrored damage and synchronized knees came from Counterpart’s foundry rite. [Armored Core VI assembly manual](https://www.fromsoftware.jp/manual/armoredcore6/ps5/customize.html) · [Official visual gallery](https://www.armoredcore.net/gallery.html)
